verdict.reasoning: Patient states decreased hearing: 'I just feel I can't really hear as well as I used to' and duration: 'Uh about six weeks.' Doctor clarifies it is the left ear: 'just the left ear, yeah.'

Intermittent decreased hearing and associated symptoms are described: 'it's kind of on and off' and 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear... and ... felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well.'
Patient notes triggers: 'It's kind of on and off. Like some things trigger it as well. So, for example, if I'm watching TV or listen to music or something that'll solve the ringing in the ear.'

No ear pain or discharge: 'have you had any pain from the ear at all? ... Uh no' and 'Any discharge coming out of the ear? No.' No chest pain or palpitations: 'Have, have you had any chest pain with it? ... No. Any palpitations...?' (no positive response). Fever not specifically reported: patient says 'Uh, not specifically apart from the dizziness so much,' indicating no clear fever.
Doctor clarifies: 'just to clarify, the difficulty you've got in hearing, is that both ears or just the left ear?' Patient: 'Uh just the left ear, yeah.' Doctor: 'Alright, so your right ear is fine.'
Past similar brief episode: 'I had something maybe, about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days, it wasn't anything as long as this.'
Cotton bud use denied: 'Now, do you use cotton ball buds to try and clean out wax from your ears?' Patient: 'Uh nah I'll do it.' (i.e., does not use them).

The transcript discusses excluding wax and other causes of muffled hearing but does not specify 'sensorineural versus conductive hearing loss' as a differential: 'Simple things might be wax... which can lead to muffled hearing... then after that, we can consider other potential possibilities.' The explicit formulation of unilateral sensorineural vs conductive hearing loss is not stated.

Left-sided tinnitus is described: 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear, uh just on the one side' and the doctor labels it: 'The ringing that you got, that you've got, it's something called Tinnitus.'
Episodic mild dizziness: 'there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well' and later 'nothing major... just a little bit kind of off balance.'

Face-to-face visit within 4–5 days for ear exam: 'maybe if we book you in for a face-to-face appointment in one of our clinics... within the next four, five days or so' and 'one of the GPs will just have a quick look in the ear and figure out whether there's physical blockage or whether there's something else going on.' This implies otoscopy and evaluation for wax or other pathology.
Tinnitus leaflet: 'I'm going to, uh, put paste the link for a leaflet about Tinnitus, um, in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it.'
Avoidance of cotton buds is reinforced: 'Now, do you use cotton ball buds...?' ... 'No, OK. Well, you're right, you should, you shouldn't be doing that. Doesn't clean up wax, it pushes it back in.'

Patient to call support line and seek earlier review if needed: 'bear with me five minutes and then you can ring the support team... they'll slot you in' and 'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to one of us over video.'
